newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares boosted by Dadas 1995 profits.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares boosted by Dadas 1995 profits.

text.p: Slovenian shares firmed 0.91 percent on Friday after market heavyweight Dadas surprised the market with a net profit for 1995.
The brokerage turned in a profit of 456.9 million tolars ($3.5 million) despite encountering problems earlier in the year.
In March, the market watchdog initialled procedures to prohibit Dadas' mutual fund Proficia Dadas from trading, claiming the fund was involved in irregular trading practices.

"Today's rise of index was mostly due to the high jump in Dadas shares. But the market is still suffering from liquidity problems, which could last until mid-September when some new shares of privatised companies are expected," one broker said.
* The seven-share SBI index rose 8.83 points to 982.42.
* Seven shares rose and seven fell, while nine were untraded.
* Turnover fell to 45.2 million tolars from 103.7 million tolars.
* Dadas was the most actively traded and was also the biggest gainer, firming 11.82 percent to 34,564 tolars on volume of 342 shares for total turnover of 11.8 million tolars.

* Ordinary shares of bank Dolenjska banka were the leading decliners, falling 4.46 percent to 10,500 tolars on volume of 78 shares for total turnover of 819,000 tolars. -- Novica Mihajlovic, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
